name: Script_ArrayCallWithElements
summary: Calls the closure in the VM's first stack slot with every element of the array in the next slot as arguments: pushes the closure, pushes each of its f_1C elements, calls Script_Vm_CallClosure with raiseerror=1 and returns 1, or -1 when the call failed.

name: maybe_Script_ArrayCallWithElementsNoThrow

name: maybe_Script_ArraySortSiftAlt

name: maybe_Script_ReturnTop

name: maybe_Script_ReturnArg2

name: maybe_Camera_FollowSelectNext
summary: Moves the follow-camera selection to the next usable entry: reads the candidate table at self->f_28->f_248 (count at +0, relative array at +4, stride 0x18), clamps/wraps the index at self+0x2C according to the direction byte self+0x3C, notifies the owner through virtual +0x8C and returns whether the index changed.
evidence: The only caller is still maybe_Camera_FollowIndexUpdate (0x00226D7C), which calls it twice as its next/previous step; no named callee and no camera class symbol appears, so the camera attribution rests on that caller.

name: maybe_Menu_StatusScreen_InitFaceAndCommands
summary: Sets up the status screen: pushes the face-icon widget, clears the face id to 0xFFFF, then fills command slots 6..9 with the texts of command ids 0x15..0x18, writes two colour/text widgets into the shared window object at +0x848/+0x950 and finally fills slot 4 with the face/expression variant id (0x23 or 0x25).
evidence: Named callees maybe_Ui_WidgetStack_PushAndInit and Ui_FaceIcon_SetId (confident) plus the func_003B3334(self, slot, id, 1) command-slot idiom fix the shape; nothing in the body creates an 'effect', which is why the old InitFaceAndEffects wording was replaced.

name: Ui_Window_ReportRecordRefCounts
summary: Fills a diagnostic window for one data record: writes four labels/layers into the window's text-arg slots, counts how many of the record's embedded u16 ids exist as items (Item_GetStoragePointer on the shared table) and how many of its embedded bytes exist in the character table (func_0066B7FC on work+0x24A98), and reports found/total into four counter widgets at +0x530/+0x638/+0x848/+0x950.
evidence: Named callees Item_GetStoragePointer and Game_GetWork confirm the two liveness tables the counters are built from; the func_00382A80(layer<<16|n, ...) text-arg idiom is the one used by Ui_Window_SetLabelText, so 'reference-count report window' is supported. It is a debug/inspection window rather than gameplay UI.

name: Ui_CharaStatusWindow_BindCharaPanes
summary: Binds the character-icon pane of the status window: picks "chara_mask" or "chara_default" from the layout depending on bit 0x10000000 of the story/system flags at work+0x2A454, binds its animation through Ui_AnimRef_Bind and resets the anim ref, then clears bit 0 of the other pane's f_44 so only one of the two is shown.
evidence: Two named callees (Ui_AnimRef_Bind, Ui_AnimRef_ResetPanes) plus the two string literals chara_mask/chara_default and the vtable 0x0075CA8C neighbour Ui_SetupCharaStatusWindow settle the pane-binding role; the leading lazy allocation of the shared 0x10-stride table is the engine's assert/table idiom that appears in dozens of functions and is not the function's purpose.

name: maybe_Gfx_ObjectWithDefaults_Ctor

The readable body is empty, so only the header's field list survives.

Returns the entry or 0.

signature: void *maybe_Container_FindBlockByOffset(void *self, void *file, int extra, u32 blockIndex, u32 offset)

name: maybe_Ui_ApplyFaceIconToWork
summary: Resolves the face/character record for self->f_14 (func_0063DF14), writes its face byte (record +9) into game work at work+0x5761, then resolves the character record (func_0063FDEC) and, when the 3D/2D mode query func_0062AB3C says 1, stores the jump-location id and the record's +10 byte into slot 8 of the work block at work+0x24A98 via func_00613354.

name: maybe_Gfx_DrawState_InitDefaults
summary: Default-initialises a 0x40-byte GPU draw-state block: runs the 12-element fixed-array default init at +4 (element ctor 0x006E7B38) and zero-fills the block, so draw passes only override the fields they use. The real entry is 0x005090F0; Ghidra's 0x00509100 is 0x10 bytes inside it.
evidence: The body is empty in readable C; the role comes from the raw disassembly and from the three named textured-draw passes (0x00567638/0x00568C90/0x00569450) that call 0x005090F0 with their local 0x40-byte state.

name: maybe_Gfx_Object_CtorFlags12
summary: Stores the owner word at +0 and default-constructs twelve one-byte flags at +4 with the empty element stub 0x006E7B38.
evidence: No caller; the element ctor 0x006E7B38 is the empty 'bx lr' stub also used by the draw-state default init, which is the only Gfx link.

name: maybe_Container_DefaultInit3x3
summary: Default-constructs three consecutive three-element byte arrays and returns the object base; in this build the element ctors (0x006E7B30/0x006E7B34) are empty stubs, so the function only performs the pointer arithmetic. The real entry is 0x005096B8; Ghidra's address is 0x10 bytes late.
evidence: No direct branch caller was found and the body is empty in readable C; only the raw disassembly (stride 1, count 3, three times) supports the shape.

name: Gfx_Movie_SubmitReadRequest
signature: void Gfx_Movie_SubmitReadRequest(u32 bufHi, u32 bufLo, int size, u8 flag)
summary: Assembles the four-word movie read request (buffer, buffer high word, size, flag) and submits it to the async archive read helper 0x00125614 with the completion callback 0x00125D84; sizes below 0xB take the stack-array path whose continuation was lost.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Gfx_Movie_ReadThread (0x00500ABC), which waits on the two handles at self+0x68 and consumes exactly this request; the request/callback pair 0x00125614/0x00125D84 is complete and visible.

name: maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots
signature: void maybe_Gfx_ModelPart_AllocSlots(GfxModelPart *self, int base, u32 count, int size, u8 mode)
summary: Carves the slot pointers of a model part out of a resource buffer: rounds size up to 16 bytes, records the per-slot strides 0x448/0xD0, fills the two pointer pairs, then constructs eight 0x20-byte elements per allocated 0x100-byte block and clears the two u16 index tables.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Gfx_ModelInstance_BuildSubBlocks (0x005324F4); the arithmetic (16-byte alignment, 0x100-byte blocks, 8 x 0x20 elements) is fully visible, the 'model part' class name is not.

name: maybe_Container_InitListObject
summary: Small list/array container constructor: installs vtable 0x00782080, builds the two self-referential link pairs, stores the owner twice, zeroes six u16 counters and constructs the inline four-byte-element array at +0x28.
evidence: No caller and no named callee; the vtable 0x00782080 has no other user in the readable tree, so neither the owner class nor the element type can be determined.

name: maybe_Gfx_ConstructMatrixSlotArray
summary: Stores the owner/type word at +0, clears the count at +4 and constructs four 0x30-byte elements at +8 with the element constructor 0x0055F4A0. 0x0055EA5C uses the same four-slot 0x30 layout for identity matrices.
evidence: No caller and no vtable; the matrix reading comes only from the 4 x 0x30 layout shared with 0x0055EA5C.

name: maybe_std_StaticInitThunk
summary: 28-byte static-initialiser thunk that tail-calls std_ConstructArray; all register arguments are still live at the tail call, so neither the global nor the element type is recoverable.
evidence: No caller, no literal and no body; the name only records that this is a compiler-emitted static array constructor, as in the other 0x005xxxxx lazy initialisers.

name: maybe_Game_InitWorkBlock
summary: Guarded one-shot initialiser of the global game-work singleton: clears the guard byte, allocates 0x2FB28 bytes aligned to 16 from the 0x00804160 pool, zeroes them and constructs the 0x1F elements of type 0x0019244C with vtable 0x00764B84.
evidence: The body is the same lazy 0x00764B84 work-block construction that appears inline in dozens of named field/event functions, so it is a game-work initialiser rather than the previous 'UI global array'; nothing in it is UI-specific.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_Entry_Ctor
summary: Stores the same byte at +0 and +1 and constructs the trailing four-element array at +2 from the element type 0x005A62EC. Too small to identify its owner; the recipe-book attribution comes only from its position between 0x005A691C and 0x005A6D18.
evidence: No caller and no named callee; the surrounding block holds the recipe-book list builders but none of them has a confident name.

name: maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_InitFromFlags
summary: Fills the horse/uma window state: after the shared work-block accessor it copies six rows of byte pairs from the work area at +0x24A98+0x57D4 into self, derives the per-row enable bytes, and stores the five global flag bytes (maybe_Flag_GetGlobalIndexed 0..4) at self+3/+7/+0xB/+0xF/+0x13.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Ui_UmaWindow_Ctor (0x004CCC34); the copy source is the work block, and the five maybe_Flag_GetGlobalIndexed reads are now recognisable as the global flag accessor, which fits 'state derived from global flags'.

name: maybe_Ui_InitStaticTable
summary: Empty 144-byte static initialiser: the readable body is a single lost std_ConstructArray() call with no recoverable arguments and no literals, so both the destination and the element type are unknown.
evidence: Still no caller, no literal and no body; the name is retained only because the address sits between the work-block initialiser 0x005A6A20 and the recipe-book ctor 0x005A6D18.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_State_Ctor
signature: void maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_State_Ctor(u8 *self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Constructor of a small state block: sets the state byte to 1, the id word to -1, two 0xFF sentinels and constructs a three-element array of the shared element type 0x00192580 at +0xA.
evidence: Its two callers are now named (maybe_Ui_TitleDemo_Init 0x001F1628 and maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_Ctor 0x001F1BEC), and the element type 0x00192580 is shared with the recipe-book material-list builder, which supports the recipe-book/demo state reading.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitByteFlagArray
summary: Child initialiser: stores the vtable and constructs a 0x20-element four-byte table at +4 (a per-slot flag/value table).
evidence: No named caller (0x005E4A78 is a thunk) and no named callee; the 0x20 x 4 layout is the only fact, which is why the name stays generic.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitWordArray5
summary: Child initialiser: stores the vtable and constructs five four-byte elements at +4 with the shared element constructor 0x006F0974 (a small fixed parameter/id table).
evidence: No named caller; 0x006F0974 is shared with the other gimmick slot builders and with maybe_Field_ActorGroup_InitFromConfig, so the subsystem fits but the table type does not.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitValuePair
summary: Child initialiser built on the shared base initialiser 0x005D451C: installs the derived vtable 0x00783F64 and constructs two four-byte values at +0xC4 with the element constructor 0x006F0958.
evidence: No caller and no named callee; the 'value pair' wording only describes the two four-byte elements, the gimmick attribution comes from the neighbouring gimmick handlers.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_InitRectPair
summary: Child initialiser built on the shared base initialiser 0x005D451C: installs the derived vtable 0x00783FC8 and constructs two 0x24-byte records at +0xC4 (the pair of rectangle/anchor descriptors used by the gimmick anchor code).
evidence: The derived vtable 0x00783FC8 has no other user and the next function (0x005D7B70) is the gimmick anchor ctor, which is what the 0x24-byte pair is for; nothing names the record type.

name: maybe_Field_Object_IsStatusFull
summary: Compares a per-id cost against a party limit: takes party member 0 through 0x0035EB98, adds 10.0 when the work flags at +0x8AB1/+0x8AB2 are set, and returns whether (item/recipe record f_C + record f_15) <= that limit. Both records come from the data manager by the low 16 bits of the id.
evidence: The caller list now includes maybe_Item_CheckCraftRequirements (0x006542CC), so the compare is a 'can this requirement be met' test rather than a status bar; the two record fields and the +10.0 bonus are visible, the quantity they measure is not.

name: maybe_Gfx_ScreenViews_ConstructArray
summary: Thin wrapper around std_ConstructArray: it constructs `count` elements at `buffer` using the element type word 0x001F2BA4, which is the pooled-record initialiser in the UI pool block.
evidence: The element constructor is now identifiable as 0x001F2BA4 (maybe_Ui_PooledRecord_ResetB), not a screen-view type, so the 'screen views' wording of the old proposal is unsupported; only the wrapper shape is certain.

name: maybe_Data_FillIndexedHandle
signature: void maybe_Data_FillIndexedHandle(u32 tag, u32 *out, void *table, int index)
summary: Fills a three-word id handle {u16 id | tag<<16, index, table word} from a record table: the id defaults to 0xFFFF and the index/word to -1, the word comes from table+0x5C and, for a non-negative index, the index and the u16 at table+index*10 are stored.
evidence: Its five callers are no longer camera-only: maybe_Ui_ApplyRowLayout (0x001D15AC) and maybe_Ui_ApplyRowLayoutDefault (0x001D15F4) use it next to the two camera helpers, so the old 'Camera_SetupSplineNode' attribution was too narrow; the handle-fill body itself is fully visible.

name: maybe_Ui_Menu_GetStateFlag
summary: Returns the byte at game-work +0x27714 as a boolean. The large prologue is only the inlined game-work accessor (the lazy 0x1F-element 0x00764B84 block), not a buffer free or a pane reset.
evidence: The readable body contains no free, no write and no pane access at all - it returns a single work byte - so the old 'ResetActivePane' name was wrong; the field itself is still only identified by its offset.

name: Ui_WorldMap_SelectLayoutName
summary: Chooses the world-map layout resource name: for the flag at game-work +0x27508 set it returns "s_world_map_b_2d.bflyt" or "s_world_map_b_3d.bflyt", otherwise "s_world_map_a_2d.bflyt" or "s_world_map_a_3d.bflyt", picked by the caller's 2D/3D argument.
evidence: The four string literals s_world_map_a_2d_bflyt / s_world_map_a_3d_bflyt / s_world_map_b_2d_bflyt / s_world_map_b_3d_bflyt and the two-level choice (work flag +0x27508, then the argument) are visible; the old 'InterpolateScroll' name described scrolling that the function never does.

name: maybe_Data_AnyRowReferencesId
summary: Tests whether any u16 id in a record's list is 'live': the list is read at record + recordIndex*4 + 8, and for each id it returns 1 as soon as the per-id flag word in the work table at +0x3AE4 is non-zero, or when one of the 0x413 rows of the data-manager table (func_0063DCA4) has that id in f_24/f_26/f_28 while the same flag is set; otherwise it returns 0.
evidence: The old 'Ui_Plate_BuildGeometry' name was plainly wrong - the body builds no geometry. What the body does is a per-id flag test plus a scan of 0x413 data-manager rows whose f_24/f_26/f_28 triple matches the id; the row table is NOT proven to be the item table (the item table has 0xB3B rows per FACTS.md), so the craft/ingredient reading is deliberately not in the name.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_InitReelStrip
summary: Initialises a 27-element four-byte reel strip in a 112-byte stack frame (element constructor 0x005F9720); the consumption of the strip happens in the caller. The 'reel strip' wording depends on that caller.
evidence: The only caller is maybe_Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult (0x0064B448) and no reel symbol table is touched here, so only the 27-entry shape is proven.

name: maybe_Casino_Slot_InitPaytable
summary: Zeroes a five-byte header (with two 0xFF sentinels) and constructs three four-byte entries in a small stack frame; the payout arithmetic is not in this function.
evidence: Same sole caller as the reel-strip init (maybe_Casino_Slot_BuildSpinResult 0x0064B448); no paytable constant or payout field is read here, so the name is a guess from the neighbour.

name: maybe_Ui_Menu_GetSubStateFlag
summary: Returns the byte at game-work +0x2FB00. The long prologue is only the inlined game-work accessor, so this is a plain state-flag getter for the menu code.
evidence: The body returns one work byte and has no side effect apart from the inlined work accessor, which supports the getter reading; nothing names the flag or its owner, and 'Check' would wrongly suggest a computed test.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_CheckCollisionBox
signature: u32 maybe_Field_Gimmick_CheckCollisionBox(void *gimmick, float *point, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, float *offset)
summary: Position test against a gimmick trigger: adds the caller's offset to the point's +0x54/+0x58 components, keeps the +0x4C/+0x50 words and passes the whole 4-element test record to the real box test at 0x006F56F4 (which is the tail the decompiler lost).
evidence: The argument tailoring to the 0x006F56F4 record is visible, but the actual dot-product/box code is inside the tail call, and the only caller (maybe_Field_Marker_UpdateScreenOffset 0x004C39B4) is unnamed.

name: maybe_Field_Gimmick_CheckInteractionZone
signature: u32 maybe_Field_Gimmick_CheckInteractionZone(void *gimmick, float *playerPos, u32 arg3, u32 arg4, float *offset)
summary: Sibling of 0x00652F48: builds the same four-element position record from the player position plus the caller offset and tail-calls 0x006F56F4, which performs the actual zone test that the decompiler lost.
evidence: Identical shape to the collision-box variant, sharing the 0x006F56F4 tail and the same caller (maybe_Field_Marker_UpdateScreenOffset); which of the two is the box and which the radius test is not distinguishable from these bodies.

name: maybe_Container_InitArray20x8
summary: Static initialiser: builds a 20-entry, 8-byte table in the static buffer at 0x007ECDA8 with the zeroing element constructor 0x00146A74 and then zeroes the tail words at +0xA0..+0xAC.
evidence: No caller and no name for the table; the readable body is empty, so this description comes from the raw disassembly and the header's literal evidence.

name: maybe_Os_InitExclusiveAccessTable
summary: Early boot initialiser: writes the eight-byte capability/count block at 0x007F2630 (0x87, 8, 10, 2, then 10/0xE/4), clears the flags at 0x007B00A4 and 0x007F2A58, takes the exclusive-access words there with LDREX/STREX and fills them with 0xFFFFFFFF, then constructs eight 0x18-byte entries at +0x2C with 0x0051CBCC.
evidence: The LDREX/STREX exclusion sequence and the 0x007B00A4 flag (also touched by the named Gfx_OpenGpuChannel/Gfx_ShutdownChannel) are visible; the 'owner table' reading still depends on the unknown element type 0x0051CBCC.

name: maybe_Data_InitPairRecords
summary: Stores the id twice and -1 at self+0/+4/+8, then constructs two 0x20-byte records in the static buffer 0x007EF0F4 with the element constructor 0x00509B1C - i.e. it initialises a global pair, not the caller object.
evidence: The array destination is the global 0x007EF0F4 (the same buffer Gfx_InitializeCommandBuffers uses), so the old 'Container_InitPair32' wording hid that the function also owns a global; the record type is still unknown.

name: maybe_Container_InitStaticStorage
summary: Static-storage initialiser: constructs the element array, loads the global head pointer at 0x00686C60, stores zero there and then registers two more globals through 0x00111E28.
evidence: No caller and no named callee; the readable body is empty, so the description comes from the raw disassembly (blx std_ConstructArray, str 0 at the head pointer, call 0x00111E28) and the element type stays unknown.

name: maybe_Container_InitArray32x16
summary: Static initialiser: constructs 0x20 elements of 0x10 bytes at the global buffer 0x007E7BE0 with the element constructor 0x005052A4, then re-points the table base.
evidence: No caller; the destination 0x007E7BE0 is also referenced by the named Fs_RegisterMountByName/Fs_UnmountByName, which hints at a file-system mount table but does not name the element type 0x005052A4.

name: maybe_Container_InitStaticArray_006A1E50
summary: Static initialiser: constructs an element array with std_ConstructArray and then writes the table base pointer, a 1 flag and two zero words into the subsystem globals (one of them gets a 0xFF sentinel).
evidence: No caller and an empty readable body; the only evidence is the raw disassembly's global stores, so the address is kept in the name to distinguish it from its twin at 0x006A5280.

name: maybe_Container_InitStaticArray_006A5280
summary: Static initialiser: constructs an element array with std_ConstructArray, zeroes the state words at buffer+0x38..+0x44 and writes several table-base pointers into globals.
evidence: No caller and an empty readable body; as with 0x006A1E50 only the raw disassembly's stores are visible, and the address suffix keeps the twin names distinct.
